title: Chocolate Walnut Granola
changes_from_base: Pressed into a firm, even sheet with a metal spatula and baked unstirred so it sets into big chunks, using oil, maple syrup and cocoa powder and brown sugar, with walnuts; chopped chocolate is tossed through once it has cooled.
summary: A dark chocolate granola with walnuts and chunks of melted chocolate stirred through after baking, creating rich pockets of flavour throughout.
equipment: large rimmed baking tray (about 33 x 46 cm)

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Heat
steps.text: Preheat the oven to 165 °C (145 °C fan) with the shelf in the upper-middle, then line a large rimmed baking tray with baking paper.

steps.title: Whisk
steps.text: In a large bowl, whisk together 120 ml vegetable oil, 80 ml maple syrup, 28 g unsweetened cocoa powder, 66 g light brown sugar, 4 tsp vanilla and ½ tsp fine salt.

steps.title: Fold
steps.text: Fold 425 g rolled oats and 225 g walnuts chopped through the chocolate mixture until every grain is well coated.

steps.title: Shape
steps.text: Tip onto the lined tray, spread into a thin layer and push down very firmly with a stiff metal spatula to form a solid, even sheet.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: Place in the oven for 40-45 min, rotating the tray at the midpoint, until the mixture feels dry and smells richly fragrant (the dark colour means you should judge by smell and touch, not appearance).

steps.title: Cool
steps.text: Let cool on a wire rack for 1 h, then break into pieces of any size.

steps.title: Finish
steps.text: Stir through 170 g dark or semi-sweet chocolate roughly chopped only once the granola is completely cold (this prevents it from melting in).

tips: Judge doneness by smell and feel rather than colour, since cocoa powder makes it naturally dark
Let the granola cool completely before stirring in chocolate so it doesn't melt and coat unevenly
Add the chocolate in chunks rather than chips so it creates satisfying pieces rather than a coating
storage: Store in an airtight container for up to 2 weeks. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
